text:
laura: quick sync / short thread. proposal: add an emergency JIT RBAC path for HSM ops that is time-limited and approver-based for BYOK rewraps. want quick feedback before i draft the PR.

chris: +1 to JIT. requirements: approver chain, MFA, session TTL, full audit export. must never export raw key material. add automatic rollback and canary gating.

anil: implementation sketch: mint ephemeral operator creds tied to an HSM attestation token. example policy snippet (pseudocode):

```json
{
  "Version":"2012-10-17",
  "Statement":[
    {
      "Effect":"Allow",
      "Action":["hsm:StartRewrap","hsm:QueryKeyState","hsm:ListKeyVersions"],
      "Resource":"arn:redwood:hsm:::customer-key/*",
      "Condition":{
        "NumericLessThanEquals":{"redwood:SessionTTLSeconds":300}
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

this would be granted only after a signed approver assertion and an active oncall session.

jess: from oncall perspective: keep friction low. i like pre-baked playbooks: approver roles vs executor roles. for P0 we aim for 30m approval SLA. also provide a single tool for exec: `rw key rewrap --customer <id> --key <id> --to <ver>` so steps are simple during incidents.

maya: legal note: obligations vary by customer. regulated tenants need chain-of-custody docs and configurable evidence retention. we need a template evidence schema that can be exported to customer audit endpoints or included in audits.

ben: vuln triage input: classify CVE actions: reboot-only, patch-without-rewrap, rewrap-required. plan: run canary rewraps on 2 low-risk tenants first, watch for errors/latency, then batch. need mapping CVE->mitigation step.

laura: two ops questions: 1) can we stream operator-level audit events to an immutable central store and optionally forward signed subsets to customers? 2) what fields do we need in the evidence bundle? i drafted a proposed minimal set below.

chris: (1) yes: central WORM-compatible S3 with object locks & signed manifests. forwarding requires mTLS and a signed subset that excludes any key material. (2) required evidence fields: operator id, approver chain, session id, HSM attestation statement, CLI args, pre/post key-hash (sha256), operation result, binary attestation blob (base64), and timestamps. include both machine-readable JSON and short human summary.

anil: example CLI capture to include in bundle: 

```
$ rw key rewrap --customer c-17 --key k-03 --to v3
REQUEST_ID=2026-06-15T03:12:11Z-6f9a
APPROVER=chris
OPERATOR=jess
SESSION_ID=sess-0a1b2c
HSM_ATTEST=attest_blob_base64
PRE_KEY_HASH=sha256:aa34...
POST_KEY_HASH=sha256:bb77...
RESULT=SUCCESS
```

store the signed approver assertion and attestation blob alongside the request log.

audit-bot: note: scheduled HSM firmware maintenance window detected: 2026-06-18 02:00-04:00 UTC. will open canary plan ticket.

deploy-bot: created INC-20260615-19 for CVE-xxxx. assigned @ben @laura.

jess: ops concerns: rewraps can cause transient errors for in-flight tokens. plan a short fallback window where we auto-failover to previous key version if errors spike >0.5%. need a non-prod rehearsal and a tabletop.

laura: action items: (A) draft RBAC change PR implementing JIT + TTL + approver flow, (B) draft evidence JSON schema & CLI capture spec, (C) coordinate canary list with @ben and @anil, (D) schedule tabletop with oncall & legal. anyone volunteer to own per-tenant retention config?

maya: legal will own per-contract retention mapping and consent flags. i'll produce a checklist and label tenants that require notification or explicit consent before rewrap.

chris: security will review PR and define signing/encryption requirements for evidence bundles. i'll also propose minimal retention durations to satisfy SOC2 & PCI and share a short policy draft.

ben: i'll pick the initial low-risk canary tenants and run the non-prod rehearsal. will share monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds.

laura: i'll open the PR this afternoon and attach the first evidence schema draft. aim to get signoffs this week so we can run the canary during the scheduled maintenance. :rocket:

mike: (note - not originally in thread) thanks everyone. if we can include a tamper-evident chain (hashes linking bundles) that will help audits.

laura: good point, mike. add hash-chain and signature to the bundle manifest.

jess: +1. also: can we include a quick command that verifies bundle integrity? `rw key verify-evidence --bundle <file>`

laura: will add verify CLI to the PR.

chris: final reminder: absolutely no plaintext key material in logs or bundles. always store hashes only.

laura: thanks all. PR incoming.
